react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on a dominant biological signal: perturbations in androgen and estrogen steroid hormone metabolism. In the multi-database RaMP ORA, the top hit was SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (FDR = 2.93e-15, fold enrichment 1668, 5 metabolites hit: estrone, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol, dihydrotestosterone). A Reactome parent pathway 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR = 1.67e-14) achieved rank 4 across 39 pathway members. The KEGG-specific MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (p = 2.51e-06, raw p = 2.5052e-06, 5/87 metabolites) as the sole significant hit. The m/z-direct mummichog network algorithm returned MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p = 8.40e-05, 12/12 compounds matched — perfect overlap) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p = 1.68e-04, 11/11 matched) as its two top-ranked pathways, providing graph-neighbourhood confirmation that the same C18-C19 steroid scaffold is central. A secondary signal around guanidinoacetic acid mapped to KEGG:hsa00260 'Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism' (p = 0.118) and KEGG:hsa00330 'Arginine and proline metabolism' (p = 0.128) via MetaboAnalystR, and to MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism via mummichog, consistent with its role as a creatine-precursor connecting amino-acid and urea-cycle pools. N-acetylgalactosamine resolved to CHEBI:506227 (N-acetyl-D-glucosamine) and enriched for aminosugar / sialic acid / heparan sulfate pathways (mummichog, p = 0.048). The six core steroid metabolites are structurally non-redundant (six distinct InChIKey block-14 clusters, zero conflicts). Driver metabolites — estrone (KEGG:C00468), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estradiol (KEGG:C00951), DHEA (KEGG:C01227), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) — collectively anchor the C21 steroid hormone biosynthesis and androgen/estrogen metabolism network and explain the treatment-vs-control metabolic divergence with FDR scores as low as 10^-15.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on a dominant biological signal centred on androgen and estrogen steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA returned 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' as the top shared pathway across SMPDB (SMPDB:SMP00068, FDR=2.93e-15) and KEGG (KEGG:map00150), with five input steroids—estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone)—hitting the 27-member pathway (fold enrichment 1668, raw p=1.26e-16). MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirmed the same KEGG namespace pathway (KEGG:hsa00140, p=2.51e-06), with the identical five steroid compounds mapped among 87 total pathway members. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.40e-05, 11/11 compounds matched) as the top-ranked network hit, and 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.40e-05, 12/12 matched) at rank 2. Guanidinoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581) independently mapped via mummichog to glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism (p=0.0329) and urea cycle/amino group metabolism (p=0.0329). N-acetylgalactosamine resolved to CHEBI:28800 but was not enriched by any of the three pathway tools.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on a dominant biological signal centred on steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-DB) returned SMPDB:SMP00356 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency as the top-ranked hit (FDR=2.93e-15, fold enrichment=1667.93, raw p=1.26e-16, 5 steroid hits among 27 pathway members). SMPDB:SMP00068 Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism and KEGG:map00150 Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism ranked second and third with identical statistics, and REACT:R-HSA-196071 Metabolism of steroid hormones appeared at rank 4 (FDR=1.67e-14, fold enrichment=1154.72, 5 steroid hits among 39 pathway members). MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 with p=4.3632e-07, matching the same five input steroids among 87 KEGG pathway members. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis identified C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.4027e-05, 12/12 compounds matched) and androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=1.68e-04, 11/11 compounds matched) as the top two network hits. All five input steroids (estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17beta-estradiol, and 17beta-hydroxy-5alpha-androstan-3-one) mapped to SMPDB:SMP00068. Guanidoacetic acid independently mapped via mummichog to Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on a dominant biological signal: perturbations in androgen and estrogen steroid hormone metabolism. In the multi-database RaMP ORA, the top hit was SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (FDR = 2.93e-15, fold enrichment 1668, 5 metabolites hit: estrone, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol, dihydrotestosterone). A Reactome parent pathway 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR = 1.67e-14) achieved rank 4 across 39 pathway members. The KEGG-specific MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (p = 2.51e-06, raw p = 2.5052e-06, 5/87 metabolites) as the sole significant hit. The m/z-direct mummichog network algorithm returned MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p = 8.40e-05, 12/12 compounds matched — perfect overlap) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p = 1.68e-04, 11/11 matched) as its two top-ranked pathways, providing graph-neighbourhood confirmation that the same C18-C19 steroid scaffold is central. A secondary signal around guanidinoacetic acid mapped to KEGG:hsa00260 'Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism' (p = 0.118) and KEGG:hsa00330 'Arginine and proline metabolism' (p = 0.128) via MetaboAnalystR, and to MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism via mummichog, consistent with its role as a creatine-precursor connecting amino-acid and urea-cycle pools. N-acetylgalactosamine resolved to CHEBI:506227 (N-acetyl-D-glucosamine) and enriched for aminosugar / sialic acid / heparan sulfate pathways (mummichog, p = 0.048). The six core steroid metabolites are structurally non-redundant (six distinct InChIKey block-14 clusters, zero conflicts). Driver metabolites — estrone (KEGG:C00468), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), estradiol (KEGG:C00951), DHEA (KEGG:C01227), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) — collectively anchor the C21 steroid hormone biosynthesis and androgen/estrogen metabolism network and explain the treatment-vs-control metabolic divergence with FDR scores as low as 10^-15.
